narrative: The model estimated a 55.6% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, it judged failure more likely than success, and that is why your law school application was rejected. The strongest factor by far was your LSAT score of 27, compared with an average of about 37 among accepted students, which pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your undergraduate GPA of 3.80, well above the accepted-student average of about 3.23; this worked in your favor and pushed toward passing. The third factor was your third-year class-rank decile of 4.00, below the accepted-student average of about 5.79, which added a smaller push toward failure. Your other background information mattered less. To move forward, ask admissions whether you can submit updated evidence, such as a stronger LSAT retake if you can prepare for it, an explanation of your third-year grades, strong letters of recommendation, or legal work experience. Consider schools that review applications holistically, and discuss whether a conditional or provisional admission path is available.
